admission.justification: The pending intent set is the part a confirmed-rows-only cap misses, and an unbounded pending set grows during exactly the interruptions the store exists to survive. The whole-store byte cases measure the document that is written rather than an approximation of it. The acknowledgement log is not capped: it reclaims by folding on observation, and the retired baseline key is not a bounded object at all, so neither is claimed here.

applicability: The disposable notice, baseline and acknowledgement working set, including interrupted intents.
conditions: Every bound is enforced over the exact serialization that is written, counting confirmed rows and pending intents together.
Shedding is oldest-first and never lets a shed intent become a notice.
Reclamation never replays what it removed.
exclusions: A canonical event journal or second history.
A cap measured on one representation and applied to another.

evidence: notes/reports/reviewer/267804e5-dd71-51e8-8f1d-d975effaaeaf/role-launch/round4/L190-fix-verification-R4.json#L190-R1-F13; Prior sealed closure retained; not reopened in fixed-list R4.

statement: The notice store that holds pending and confirmed terminal notices enforces count and byte bounds over everything it writes, pending intents included.
